solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mellor in trouble about words addressed to someone? He should be setting an example!

definitions.text: He should be setting an example!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters wrap around the poem
a name in trouble is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem often addressed to a person or thing

explanation.surface: A disgraced politician named Mellor, caught in a scandal, is ironically told he ought to be a good example to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' makes ROLEML, which 'about' wraps round the poem. David Mellor, a former Conservative minister, was recorded ranting at a London taxi driver in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looked up to and imitated by others is expected to set an example for them.

clue.text: Alien spy barred with no hint of diplomacy after Russia's initial expression of disapproval

indicators.note: after places the anagram behind the opening letter
initial picks the opening letter of the word Russia's
alien means strange or foreign, so these letters are made strange by rearranging
with no means the word barred loses a letter
a hint is a small trace, here the first letter of diplomacy

explanation.surface: A foreign spy is banned undiplomatically, and Russia responds with disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no hint of' leaves BARRE; 'Alien' shuffles the pool to ASPBERRY. Britain's slang for a rude noise is to blow one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing a raspberry is a rude noise made with the tongue and lips to show contempt.

clue.text: Gather pound's to gain

parts.note: L stands for libra, the pound sterling
to earn is to gain money by work

explanation.surface: A cryptic order to collect pounds in order to make a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather a fact is to infer or find it out, a sense of coming to know.

clue.text: Conscious uncoupling method from Martin leads to divorce for up-to-date lovers

indicators.note: uncoupling means detaching, so a word is detached from the name Martin

parts.note: an art is a skill or method of doing something

indicators.note: leads are the front letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin famously announced their split as a 'conscious uncoupling'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncoupling ... from' removes ART from MARTIN, leaving MIN; the leads of divorce, for, up-to-date, lovers give DFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being mindful of something is being aware or conscious of it, a near synonym.

clue.text: Stupid, heartless Russian leader pointlessly intervening to take over?

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the trimmed leader sits inside the trimmed adjective
heartless removes the central letter of the word for stupid

parts.note: dense means slow-witted or stupid

indicators.note: N is a compass point, so pointlessly drops it

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian president

explanation.surface: A dim, cold-hearted Putin is pictured meddling in order to seize control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves DESE, 'pointlessly' drops N (a compass point), and 'intervening' sets the shortened leader inside. Putin's takeover in 2014 was of Crimea (23 down).
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a substitute, temporarily standing in for someone and doing their job.

clue.text: Rump of voters supporting a party caught between Left and Right — they've few friends

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath
caught between puts something in the gap between two letters

parts.note: a party is a single person, as in a party to a contract, so one

indicators.note: the rump is the hind end, here the final letter of voters

explanation.surface: A political party squeezed between left and right finds itself with few allies at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a party' is a person in the legal sense, giving ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary people who prefer their own company are those with few friends.

clue.text: Islamist group Egypt's leader rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the name is read from end to start

parts.note: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi is the president of Egypt

explanation.surface: Egypt's president turns his back on a militant Islamist movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The jihadist organisation also called Islamic State was widely known by this acronym in 2014.

clue.text: Property slowdown's beginning — can bust develop before second quarter of year?

indicators.note: before places the shuffled letters ahead of the last piece
beginning picks the opening letter of slowdown's
develop means grow into a new form, so these letters are reshaped
year has four letters, so its second quarter is its second letter

explanation.surface: A housing-market slowdown raises the fear of a bust taking shape early in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' rearranges CAN BUST to UBSTANC.
explanation.definitionFit: A property or substance of something is its essential matter or quality; also wealth, as in a man of substance.

clue.text: I say war terminally ruining country

indicators.note: ruining wrecks the letters, so they are rearranged
terminally picks the final letter of war

explanation.surface: A lament that war is destroying a country, all too apt for Syria in 2014.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruining' rearranges I SAY plus R, the end of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern state bordering Turkey, Iraq and Lebanon, an example of a country.

clue.text: England exiting the cup's terrible shock to the system?

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
exiting means leaving, so one letter departs from the phrase

explanation.surface: England crashing out of the World Cup is a terrible shock to the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exiting' takes E from THE CUPS, leaving THCUPS; 'terrible' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent seizure of government is a jolt to the political system, cleverly cast as a shock.

clue.text: It's a wrench when king or queen abdicates in monarchy

indicators.note: abdicates means steps down from the throne, so the royal letter departs

parts.note: a sprain is a wrench of a joint
R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: Giving up a crown is a painful wrench for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: King Juan Carlos of Spain abdicated in 2014 in favour of his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain is a kingdom, an example of a country ruled as a monarchy.

clue.text: Photo opens with this popular figure's access code

indicators.note: opens picks the first letter of Photo

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a number is a figure

explanation.surface: A celebrity's personal security code opens their private photo collection.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2014 celebrities' phones were hacked and private photos published.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal identification number is the secret code that grants access to a card or phone.

clue.text: Ure and Geldof lately in money spinning successor to Live Aid

indicators.note: successor to means coming after, so the rest follows the verb for live

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: in places the final letters inside the reversed money
spinning turns the word for money right round

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: lately picks the final letters of Ure and Geldof

explanation.surface: Midge Ure and Bob Geldof stage a money-raising follow-up to the Live Aid concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live Aid' looks like one name but splits: 'Live' is wordplay and 'Aid' the definition. 'spinning' makes NIT, which 'in' fills with E and F (picked by 'lately') to give NEFIT; 'successor to' puts it after.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid in the sense of help or advantage; also a benefit concert raises aid.

clue.text: Ancient stone picked up on tail of comet reflecting indication of position in space

parts.note: rose means got up or picked up

indicators.note: the tail is the last letter of comet
reflecting means mirrored, so the two letters are turned round

parts.note: at is a preposition indicating position

explanation.surface: The Rosetta space probe touched down on a comet's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rosetta Stone, key to hieroglyphs, gave its name to the probe that landed on a comet in 2014; 'in space' nods to that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rosetta Stone is the ancient inscribed slab that unlocked Egyptian writing.

clue.text: Maybe to exercise damage limitation with defecting MP is rash

definitions.meaning: read as wreck-less, doing less wrecking
Mark ..., the MP who left the Tories for UKIP in 2014

explanation.surface: A defecting MP tries to limit the damage, which seems unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Reckless defected from the Conservatives to UKIP and won the Rochester and Strood by-election.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless of danger and careless of results is the everyday meaning of rash.

clue.text: Persuaded Cable to enter Conservative deal initially

indicators.note: to enter means to go into, so the politician's name goes inside
initially picks the first letter of deal

parts.note: Vince Cable was a Liberal Democrat minister in the coalition

explanation.surface: Vince Cable is won over to join the Conservatives in a coalition deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made sure of something by argument; brought round, a synonym of persuaded.

clue.text: Give hint of criticism for basic hotel facilities?

parts.note: to hand is to give

indicators.note: a hint is a trace, here the first letter of criticism

explanation.surface: A guest offers a little criticism about a hotel's bare amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation means hot and cold running water, once advertised in modest British hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot and cold taps are the most elementary amenity a cheap lodging could boast of.

clue.text: Change of heart in region seeking independence results in apparent paralysis

indicators.note: a change of heart alters the central letter of the region's name

parts.note: Catalonia is the Spanish region campaigning for independence

explanation.surface: A shift in the mood of a separatist region leaves it seemingly frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter L of CATALONIA becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic state is a stupor in which a person seems unable to move, a seeming immobility.

clue.text: Nice, perhaps, women at church exalting the Lord

indicators.note: exalting means raising up, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: God is the Lord

explanation.surface: Women at church in the French city of Nice raise praise to God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city but is NICE, the body that rules on NHS treatments.
explanation.definitionFit: NICE, the UK health-care body, is an example of a regulator or official guardian of standards.

clue.text: UK less united after no vote returned by Scots finally exerts pull

indicators.note: after places the shortened kingdom behind the reversed vote
returned means sent back, so the vote word is read from end to start

parts.note: nay is a vote against

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is taken away
finally picks the last letter of Scots

explanation.surface: After Scotland votes no, the United Kingdom stays together but less united, a nod to the 2014 referendum.
explanation.walkthrough: As first printed the clue had no definition; the setter later restored 'exerts pull' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to tug sharply, so a person who does so is pulling hard.

clue.text: Upcoming vehicles have built-in autonomous technology at the outset and computer guidance

indicators.note: built-in means fitted inside, so the opening letters go into the reversed vehicles
upcoming in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: vans are vehicles

indicators.note: at the outset picks the first letters of autonomous and technology

explanation.surface: New vehicles are to come with self-driving technology and computerised navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite navigation system is a device that directs a driver by computer.

clue.text: US and allies introducing smart arms funded by this?

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the word for smart goes inside

parts.note: the West means the US and its allies
arch means cunning or knowing

explanation.surface: America and its allies bring in smart weapons, paid for from a fighting fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund set aside to pay for a military campaign.

clue.text: Prisoner — any of three from Al Jazeera in can, shut up

parts.note: a con is a convict or prisoner

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the word for can

parts.note: a tin is a can

parts.words: any of three from Al Jazeera
parts.note: Al Jazeera ... three letter As, any of which will do

explanation.surface: Al Jazeera journalists jailed in Egypt in 2014 were prisoners shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something enclosed or confined, as in holding back a feeling.

clue.text: Illegal act on a peninsula

parts.note: a crime is an illegal act

explanation.surface: A reference to the illegal annexation of a peninsula by Russia in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea land mass annexed by Russia is an example of a peninsula.

clue.text: Social network to have a laugh about white van

indicators.note: about means around, so the laughing verb surrounds the letter

parts.note: to titter is to laugh nervously

indicators.note: the van is the front, so it picks the first letter of white

explanation.surface: People on social media mock a photo of a white van, as in the 2014 tweet by an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour's Emily Thornberry tweeted a white van photo during the Rochester by-election.
explanation.definitionFit: A microblogging site where users post short messages is an online social network.

clue.text: Burning in art school

indicators.note: burning sets the letters on fire, scattering them into a new order

explanation.surface: A fire breaks out in an art school, as at Glasgow's in 2014.
explanation.walkthrough: The Glasgow School of Art was badly damaged by fire in 2014.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or coach them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Conservative leader in thrall to anti-European magnetism? A fanciful notion!

indicators.note: in thrall to means subject to, so the leading letter follows behind

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Conservative

parts.note: it means sex appeal or personal magnetism

explanation.surface: A Tory leader attracted by Eurosceptic charisma is a fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A conceit is an elaborate or fanciful idea, a metaphysical poets' term for an ingenious image.

clue.text: Taken a mistress disguised to the Elysee as a friend

definitions.text: to the Elysee as a friend

indicators.note: disguised means concealed within the phrase

explanation.surface: The French president, of the Elysee Palace, has taken a mistress and passes her off as a mere friend.
explanation.walkthrough: President Hollande's affair was exposed in 2014; the Elysee is the French president's palace, so the phrase is French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French words for a companion: a pal, in the language spoken at the Elysee.

clue.text: Hailed by excited media, more than half of Clacton's turned out …

indicators.note: turned out means overturned, so these letters are rearranged
more than half takes the first four of the seven letters
excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The media enthuse as Clacton's voters turn out in force, a nod to the 2014 UKIP by-election win.
explanation.definitionFit: Being praised publicly and enthusiastically is to be acclaimed, a synonym of hailed.

clue.text: … a seat changing hands once more

parts.note: in an election a seat won from another party is a gain

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a seat changes hands at a by-election.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetition: doing something another time, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Signals assent to ban on games console?

parts.note: no as in no smoking signals a ban
the DS is a Nintendo handheld games console

explanation.surface: A parent agrees to a ban on a child's games console.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving the head up and down is a gesture that shows agreement.

clue.text: Head of Top Gear in an awkward state

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the head is the first letter of Top

explanation.surface: The Top Gear presenter gets into an awkward situation in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2014 the BBC's Top Gear team had to flee Argentina over a number plate seen as mocking the Falklands War.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American republic is an example of a sovereign nation.
